questions.q: What does this lesson recommend regarding which Trailhead Playground to use across this entire career path?
options: Reuse one playground (from Lesson 3) across courses, unless there's a specific reason not to
Create a brand-new playground for every single lesson
Use a different playground for every course with no exceptions
Never log back into the same playground twice
questions.explain: The lesson recommends reusing one playground across courses, since fragmenting work across many orgs costs more than a busier single org does.

questions.q: What does Rename actually change, according to this lesson?
options: Only the display label on the Hands-On Orgs page — it doesn't affect the org's login username
The org's login username, requiring a new password
The org's Organization Edition
Nothing — Rename is purely cosmetic and has no effect at all
questions.explain: Rename only updates the label shown on Hands-On Orgs; it's safe to use any time since it doesn't touch the actual login username.

questions.q: What does the "Install a Package" tool mentioned in this lesson do?
options: Installs an app or package into the Trailhead Playground when you paste in its package ID
Permanently deletes installed packages from an org
Only works in paid production orgs, never in a Trailhead Playground
Resets the org back to a blank state
questions.explain: The Install a Package tool lets you paste in a package ID to install it directly into your Trailhead Playground.

questions.q: When a package install asks "where do you want to install this package," why does this lesson say a personal training playground counts as the "Production" option?
options: Because there is no sandbox tier underneath a personal training org — sandboxes only exist under a real company's production org
Because Trailhead Playgrounds are technically paid Enterprise Edition orgs
Because "Production" and "Sandbox" mean the exact same thing in this context
Because Salesforce requires all package installs to go into production
questions.explain: Since sandboxes only exist in relation to a company's real production org (per Lesson 5), a personal playground has no sandbox tier, making it the Production option by default.

questions.q: Why does this lesson suggest logging into your permanent playground periodically, even when you're not actively using it for a lesson?
options: Because long stretches of total inactivity can cause a playground to go stale
Because Salesforce charges a fee for inactive orgs
Because Trailhead automatically deletes playgrounds after one login
Because periodic logins are required to keep Trailhead badges from expiring
questions.explain: The lesson notes that long inactivity can cause a playground to go stale, so periodic logins (a monthly reminder, for example) help keep it active.
